overview: A membrane keypad packs 16 buttons (in a 4x4 grid) into a flexible plastic sheet, but connects to a microcontroller with only 8 wires instead of 16 — the trick is that buttons are wired in a row/column matrix, and software scans one row at a time to see which column(s) register a press, deducing exactly which button was pressed from the row+column combination. That row/column scanning approach is a genuinely important pattern worth understanding, since it's how far larger button/LED matrices (keyboards, LED walls) stay wire-efficient too.
simpleSummary: A flat sheet of 16 buttons wired so only 8 wires are needed to know which one was pressed.

specifications.interface: 8 pins total (4 row + 4 column), scanned in software — no onboard driver chip
specifications.construction: Flexible membrane/PET film with printed conductive traces, no mechanical click
specifications.ratedVoltage: Logic-level, no specific voltage rating needed (purely passive contacts)

pinMap.name: R1
pinMap.function: Row 1 — driven LOW (or read) in turn while scanning columns to detect a press in this row.

pinMap.name: C1
pinMap.function: Column 1 — read (with a pull-up/down) while a row is actively driven, to detect a press at that row/column intersection.
pinMap.gotcha: Uses all 8 pins even though it looks like it should need fewer — this is the standard matrix-scanning tradeoff: fewer wires than one-pin-per-button, but not zero.

useCases.title: PIN code entry / security system
useCases.scenario: Enter a numeric code to unlock a door or disarm an alarm.

useCases.title: Menu navigation input
useCases.scenario: 16 distinct keys for navigating menus or entering values on a standalone device.

useCases.title: Simple calculator/data entry device
useCases.scenario: Numeric and function key input for a custom standalone gadget.

oftenConfusedWith: Individual tactile switches (simpler for a few buttons, but doesn't scale to 16 without matrix wiring anyway)
oftenUpgradedTo: Capacitive touch keypads for a sealed, more durable interface
